subject: history_social
passage: Göbekli Tepe, a hilltop site in southeastern Turkey, has forced archaeologists to rethink the origins of monumental building. Raised around 9500 BCE, thousands of years before the invention of writing or the wheel, ______ The builders appear to have been hunter-gatherers, a conclusion that challenges the long-held view that only settled farming societies could organize projects on such a scale.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: visitors to the site can see massive T-shaped limestone pillars, some taller than five meters, carved with foxes, boars, and vultures.
choices.B: the carvings of foxes, boars, and vultures cover massive T-shaped limestone pillars at the site, some taller than five meters.
choices.C: archaeologists have found massive T-shaped limestone pillars at the site, some taller than five meters, carved with foxes, boars, and vultures.
choices.D: the site's massive T-shaped limestone pillars, some taller than five meters, are carved with foxes, boars, and vultures.

explanation.why: An introductory modifier describes whatever noun comes right after the comma. "Raised around 9500 BCE" describes something that was set upright long ago, which can only be the stone pillars. So the subject that follows must be the pillars themselves.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Placing "visitors" right after the modifier says modern visitors were raised around 9500 BCE, which makes no sense.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The subject "the carvings" comes right after the modifier, but carvings are cut into stone, not raised; the modifier is meant for the pillars.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Placing "archaeologists" right after the modifier says the archaeologists were raised around 9500 BCE, so the modifier dangles.
explanation.D: Correct. The subject "the site's massive T-shaped limestone pillars" comes right after the modifier, so the pillars are what was raised around 9500 BCE.
